date.as_written: śrīnepālasamvatsaragate 900 śrāvaṇaśulkatṛtīyāyāṃ tīthau (!) uttarabhadraṇakṣatre (!) dhṛtiyoge śukravāsare

notes: śrīdivākarāya rastu (!) likely represents an auspicious wish for a human beneficiary/owner named Divākara (i.e. śrīdivākarāyāstu), though it could alternatively be a corrupt invocation to the deity Divākara (the Sun). A verse on weapons cited from Svarodaya is appended after the completion statement.
